title: Extra Work Approval
summary: Agree on the extra work before it starts. A focused scope, additional price, customer response, and versioned record for the contractor's next change request.
problem: A customer's while-you-are-here request can leave extra scope, added cost and timing scattered across a conversation before either person has a clear record.
contribution: Aaron defined a narrow contractor-to-customer workflow and directed the product's private access boundary, immutable versions, response clarity and distinctive work-order notebook design.
solution: The contractor prepares one change request with scope, price and declared timing, publishes a private review link, and keeps the customer's response connected to that exact version.
outcomes: A fictional $350 side-gate request passed deployed protected publication, independent customer approval, owner recovery, matching exports and reload persistence; the synthetic workspace was then deleted.
Separate local Workers/D1 tests verified declined and changes-requested outcomes without granting approval.
